forecaster_note: Winds light and calm at dawn, cleaning up a nice shot of short-period E/NE swell, with a touch of S swell for a couple of wedgey options on the exposed beaches. The magnets are fun, picking up a few head-high sets and hollowing out toward low. A late southerly change will limit clean options to the southern corners — get amongst it early. Mon: peaky head-high S + E/NE mix, light AM winds. Wed looks like a skip. — Surfline forecaster (Sun 4 Oct)

wind.summary: Light W 9 kph offshore at dawn, WNW 13 kph by 10am, light and variable at 1pm, then SE onshore ~20 kph from 4pm with a late southerly change.

days.label: Today
days.note: Clean start: light W offshore, NE 6ft @ 8s (~535 kJ) plus a touch of SE and tiny S. Go 7–10am before the winds ease; Long Reef and Curl Curl rate best (fair-good). SE onshore ~20 kph from 4pm with a late southerly change. Low 8:39am, high 3:19pm.

swells.label: Dominant short-period NE swell — the good angle
Secondary SE swell — adds peaky wedge energy
Tiny long-period S (dead-S angle, wraps poorly at Dee Why)

dee-why.window: Light W offshore at first light, WNW 13 kph by 10am — clean through the morning, tide dropping to the 8:39am low. SE onshore ~20 kph from 4pm. NE 55° is the right angle; the S component is tiny.

tip.label: Frontside rights at the Point
tip.text: Short-period NE is the right angle — frontside rights at the Point, backside lefts on the beach peaks. 8s is punchy not powerful: stay on the drive and take the N corner.

long-reef.window: Picks up the most size and rates best (fair-good). Offshore W early and through ~10am, hollowing toward the 8:39am low. Southerly change late — get in before it.

tip.label: Frontside rights off the reef
tip.text: Chest to overhead and hollowing at low. Sit deep on the peak, commit to the drop and take the wedgey sections on your forehand.

curl-curl.window: Light offshore to 10am, fair-good rating early. Peaky banks; N end cleanest as the S change arrives.

tip.label: Find the bank
tip.text: Peaky and fun — find the bank holding shape and take the shoulder. Good flowy session board.

manly.window: Smallest of the four but clean with W offshore early. North Steyne is mostly a fun-wave option. Manly had a drone sighting yesterday — shark status updating shortly.

tip.label: North Steyne peaks
tip.text: Thigh to waist and clean — a groveller-friendly morning. Pick the best peak and keep it simple.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Peaky S + E/NE short-period mix for head-high surf at most breaks; light W offshore in the morning (7 kph), onshore ESE later. Fair-good at Dee Why, Curl Curl and Manly from ~7–10am. Short-period S can wedge — pick the north-facing corners.

dee-why.window: Light W offshore 7–10am; onshore ESE from midday. Sneaky S swell wraps poorly — N corner.

long-reef.window: Most size again; peaky head-high at the reef in the light AM winds.

manly.window: Fair-good early with the light W; smaller than the northern spots.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Rest of Sunday: offshore through ~10am, light and variable at 1pm, then SE onshore ~20 kph from 4pm and a late southerly change — afternoon rating drops to poor-fair. Just past the weekend: Mon head-high and clean AM, Tue easing ENE waist–chest with morning offshores, Wed large onshore S — likely a skip.
